options.content: **Flow Designer** draws node/edge diagrams with glowing edges and travelling particles. Nodes show the last value of a bound field (unit and decimals from standard options); edges can map a field to particle speed, colour (via thresholds) or width. Edit a panel and turn on *Layout → Edit layout* to drag nodes, draw edges and reshape curves.

panels.title: Design mode (Edit layout on) - drag things!

options.content:
### Data-driven diagrams
The panels below are built from query results instead of being drawn: any frame with `source`/`target` fields (or series with those labels) becomes edges, nodes are laid out automatically (layered or radial), and values drive particle speed, colour or width. The right-hand panel shows **Data + manual overrides**: a few nodes were dragged and restyled; everything else still follows the data.

panels.title: No query · demo data
panels.description: This panel's query returns no data (TestData 'No data points'; an empty target list would be replaced by a default random walk). Diagram source = Data and Data → Demo data = When no data (the default) build a generated 12-node service graph through the normal field pipeline, with a 'Demo data' badge. Add a query with source/target rows and the real result takes over; set Demo data to Off to see the empty state instead.

panels.title: Fresh panel · manual source, empty diagram, no query
panels.description: Exactly what a newly added Flow Designer looks like: Diagram source = Manual, nothing drawn, no data. With Demo data on, the generated graph stands in (laid out as in Data mode) with a one-line hint until you load the example, draw a diagram, or switch the source to Data. Turning on Edit layout shows the real empty canvas.
